service.description: The draft of a time import of the current user: the draft map (empty when there is none, or the id is not a draft id), the location of its file, and the folder.

actions.script: draft = {} found = false fileLocation = null const userId = ec.user.userId if (!userId || !importId || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/.test(String(importId))) return folder = `dbresource://ironstone/TimeImport/${userId}/${importId}` const text = ec.resource.getLocationReference(folder + '/draft.json').getText() if (!text) return try { draft = JSON.parse(text) || {} } catch (err) { ec.logger.warn(`Time import ${importId} of ${userId}: the draft does not read: ${err}`); draft = {}; return } found = true fileLocation = folder + '/source.csv'

service.description: Merges the fields given into the draft of a time import of the current user and saves it.

The import's first step: the file (an upload, or the file already in the draft when none is given) read as text in its character set (mantle.party.ContactImportServices.read#ContactFileText) and kept as the draft's source file, checked by a preview of its first row (its columns: a date, and hours or start and end), and the person of the rows that name none (the user, or a person whose weeks the user approves). A new import gets an id; the same importId replaces its file.
The preview step: the draft's file planned without writing (import#TimeEntryCsv preview), the first 50 rows with their texts and the counts over the whole file.

The import's last step: mantle.work.TimeServices.import#TimeEntryCsv of the draft's file (each row in its own transaction: a row that fails is named with its reason and the rest are imported), the result kept in the draft (counts, the failures with their reasons and values, the warnings) for the result view and the failures download. A file of up to 200 rows is imported in the request; a larger one (or background true) runs on as a job (run#ImportNow): the draft is running, the user gets the progress on the topic timeImportProgress (progressKey the importId), and the draft ends done or failed. An import running or done is not started again.

Imports the draft's file now (for run#Import, in the request or as its job, as the user who started it), then the draft done with its result. An import that stops (an error before the rows) leaves the draft failed with the error, never running, so it can be run again.
